title: POC scoping: anchor-prompt quality plan & load estimates - Boreal Systems
next_steps: Deliver preliminary load estimate and cost bands
Share SOC2 and VPC deployment checklist
Schedule 60-min technical runthrough with infra team next week
action_items: Marcus Lee | Upload initial benchmark harness (locust + sample prompts) to shared folder | 2026-04-16
Alex Moreno | Provide 1 week of real traffic histograms and token distribution csv | 2026-04-15
Priya Shah | Send proposal draft and pricing bands for Dedicated vs Hosted POC | 2026-04-18
summary: AE+SE kicked off POC scoping focused on a 4-week quality + perf evaluation. Agreed to use an 'anchor prompt' set (customer-provided + Redwood-suggested variants), define regression harness, hallucination checks, format validators, and a composite scoring rubric. Initial load target: 400 rps peak with 150 token avg per request; Redwood to provide benchmark harness and cost bands. Security questions around VPC and KMS noted; Redwood to share SOC2 docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll try to keep this to ~45 minutes and land on concrete next steps. Marcus and Evelyn are with me from Redwood. Alex, want to kick off with goals from Boreal?
[00:18] Alex Moreno: Yeah, hi. Our main thing is quality gating — we need to make sure generated config snippets and analyst summaries are accurate and follow our formatting rules, low hallucination, and predictable cost. We're considering both Redwood hosted and Dedicated. Timeline is tight — product wants a decision in 6 weeks.
[00:36] Marcus Lee: Great. For the POC we typically split quality + perf. For quality we'll build an anchor prompt set — think of these as canonical prompts with variations, golden outputs and negative cases. We'll run regression harnesses against model variants and measure pass/fail and semantic similarity.
[00:54] Jordan Kim: Quick question on anchor prompts — do you expect us to craft them or you?
[00:58] Priya Shah: Both. We'll provide Redwood templates and examples, you provide customer-specific ones. Preferably we get 50-100 core anchors, with 3-5 paraphrases each.
[01:15] Samira Patel: That's a lot — can we do 30 anchors and iterate?
[01:19] Marcus Lee: Absolutely. Start with 30 high-priority anchors that cover the most common workflows. We'll augment with paraphrases and adversarial variants.
[01:28] Liam O'Neill: Security - we need to know data residency, KMS integration, audit logs — can Redwood do private deployments with our KMS?
[01:35] Evelyn Park: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM for on-prem and VPC options. We'll share the SOC2 + architecture checklist after the call.
[01:44] Alex Moreno: Excellent. For success criteria, I'd like explicit thresholds. e.g., hallucination rate < 2%, format pass-rate > 95%, semantic similarity > 0.85. Thoughts?
[01:54] Marcus Lee: Those are reasonable as starting targets. For semantic similarity we use embed-based cosine with a threshold you can tune; we also include exact token checks for strict outputs like JSON config. For hallucination detection we'll run a combination: entity-checker against a whitelist + model uncertainty heuristics and a human-reviewed sample to calibrate.
[02:15] Priya Shah: Important to note — hallucination definition for you is what? Incorrect facts, extraneous invented steps, or both?
[02:22] Alex Moreno: Primarily incorrect facts and invented dependencies that could misconfigure infra.
[02:28] Marcus Lee: OK, we'll prioritize entity consistency and schema adherence checks. For schema/format validation we'll use a JSON schema and a small regex-based sanity layer for the outputs that look like manifests.
[02:40] Priya Shah: On the benchmarking side — what's your load today and what do you expect at peak?
[02:46] Alex Moreno: Current internal tooling is low volume, ~50 rps during business hours. We want to size for production: spike to 400 rps with bursts to 700 for scheduled runs. Average request token length is around 150 tokens, but the summaries can get to 400 tokens occasionally.
[03:06] Marcus Lee: Noted. For perf evaluation we'll run two phases: synthetic stress (locust) to validate latency tails and tokens/sec, and replay of anonymized production traces to validate real distribution. We'll target p95 latency < 250ms for short prompts, and document latency for long generations.
[03:22] Jordan Kim: Replay — we'll need guidance on anonymization.
[03:26] Evelyn Park: We'll send a template to transform user identifiers and redact PII.
[03:31] Samira Patel: How do you handle caching? We do many repeated prompts across analysts.
[03:35] Marcus Lee: Redwood runtime has prefix/KV caching and you can opt into caching rules. For the POC we'll instrument cache hit rate and simulate realistic cache priming. That affects cost significantly.
[03:47] Alex Moreno: Cost bands — can you give rough numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated for our workload?
[03:50] Priya Shah: We'll provide ranges after we run a small perf probe, but rule of thumb: Hosted is higher per-token but lower fixed overhead; Dedicated has commit and predictable throughput. We'll put together three sizing scenarios based on your 400 rps target: conservative, expected, and aggressive.
[04:06] Liam O'Neill: On compliance, how do you surface access logs and audit trails?
[04:10] Evelyn Park: Console exposes token-level cost/latency breakdowns and we can push audit logs to your SIEM. For Private, logs remain in your VPC. We'll include a sample log schema.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: Back to quality tests — scoring approach proposal: composite score = 0.5 * semantic_similarity + 0.2 * format_pass + 0.2 * hallucination_penalty + 0.1 * human_review_adjustment. Hallucination_penalty reduces score where entity mismatches found. We can adjust weights per anchor.
[04:41] Samira Patel: Can we include brittle negative tests — e.g., adversarial prompts that historically break other models?
[04:46] Marcus Lee: Yes, we'll include adversarial set and a severity label so failures can be triaged.
[04:51] Alex Moreno: How often will you run regressions? Daily or on new model rollouts?
[04:55] Marcus Lee: For the POC we'll run nightly regression runs and seed a daily sample for human spot-checks. For production we recommend on every model change or weekly batch runs.
[05:06] Priya Shah: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week): anchor prompt transfer + traffic histograms. Week 1: Redwood builds harness and baseline runs on chosen open model(s). Week 2: Customer review of results and iterate anchors. Week 3: Load test with replay and caching enabled. Week 4: Final scoring, runbook, and decision meeting.
[05:24] Jordan Kim: That fits our 6-week decision window.
[05:27] Alex Moreno: Do you need any infra access for Dedicated POC?
[05:30] Marcus Lee: For Dedicated we'll need network peering and port access; for Hosted no infra changes but we may request a test API key and allowlist. We'll send a checklist.
[05:41] Liam O'Neill: On encryption, can keys stay in our KMS?
[05:43] Evelyn Park: Yes for Redwood Private. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS; Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys unless you opt into bring-your-own-key in supported regions.
[05:53] Samira Patel: What's the human review cadence and size?
[05:56] Priya Shah: For calibration we usually do 100 human-labeled examples across positive/negative anchors, then 20 per day for spot checks during the POC.
[06:07] Alex Moreno: OK let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:10] Priya Shah: Marcus will upload a benchmark harness and anchor template. Alex will provide traffic histograms and initial 30 anchors. I'll draft a proposal and pricing. Evelyn will share SOC2 and deployment checklist.
[06:22] Alex Moreno: Great. Any final Qs?
[06:24] Samira Patel: None from me. Thanks.
[06:26] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the infra deep dive.
[06:32] [call ends]
